To confirm, you're seeing these errors when restarting Home Assistant?

I see similar, but I'm thinking it's not just at restart. Here's an error message. If there are others I can add to help, please let me know.

````
Logger: homeassistant.components.tplink_omada.coordinator
Source: components/tplink_omada/update.py:47
Integration: TP-Link Omada (documentation, issues)
First occurred: August 1, 2023 at 4:29:16 PM (10 occurrences)
Last logged: August 3, 2023 at 10:29:16 PM

Unexpected error fetching Omada API Data - Firmware Updates data: 'needUpgrade'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/update_coordinator.py", line 283, in _async_refresh
    self.data = await self._async_update_data()
                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/tplink_omada/coordinator.py", line 41, in _async_update_data
    return await self.poll_update()
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/tplink_omada/update.py", line 65, in poll_update
    return {d.device.mac: d for d in await self._get_firmware_updates()}
                                     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/tplink_omada/update.py", line 43, in _get_firmware_updates
    updates = [
              ^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/tplink_omada/update.py", line 47, in <listcomp>
    if not d.need_upgrade
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/tplink_omada_client/devices.py", line 103, in need_upgrade
    return self._data["needUpgrade"]
           ~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
KeyError: 'needUpgrade'
```

This looks like a compatibility issue with the controller or one of the devices attached to it. Can you confirm the firmware/software version of the Omada controller you are using, and what omada devices (e.g. access points, switches, etc) you have connected to it? I will need to put in a fix to ignore the missing "needUpgrade" field, so updates just won't work for those devices, but it would be nicer if I could remove the entity altogether if I know it won't support updates. It would be super helpful if you could get the device list response that the controller sends to the Omada web interface. To get this, open the Chrome developer tools (F12), and look in the Network tab. Then then log in to the Omada controller page. When you open the Devices page on your Site (not the Global Organization view), you should see a request for a page called "devices": If you click on that, and select the "Response" tab, it should show you all of the data that the API has: If you could copy that text into this issue (redact anything you don't want to share), it would be most helpful!

I think I know what it is - while the devices are rebooting they go through a number of different states like "REBOOTING" and "ADOPTING", during which the data that is returned for them is reduced. The code already checks that the status is "CONNECTED", but it doesn't seem like this is enough. The value might appear once some background upgrade check has happened on the controller. I'll put in a fallback so it assumes there is no upgrade if the `needUpgrade` value is missing.
